query: In which county is the English king Harold Godwinson buried?

pipeline_result.response: The answer to this question is: "England."
retrieved_context: Edith the Fair: Edith the Fair (Old English: "Ealdgȳð Swann hnesce" , "Edyth the Gentle Swan"; c. 1025 – c. 1086), also known as Edith Swanneck, was the first wife of King Harold Godwinson.  "Swanneck" (or Swan-Neck) comes from the folk etymology which made her in Old English as "swann hnecca", "swan neck", which was actually most likely a corrupted form of "swann hnesce, ""Gentle Swan"" ".  She is sometimes confused with Ealdgyth, daughter of Earl Ælfgar of Mercia, who was queen during Harold's reign.

Tostig Godwinson: Tostig Godwinson ( 1026 – 25 September 1066) was an Anglo-Saxon Earl of Northumbria and brother of King Harold Godwinson.  After being exiled by his brother, Tostig supported the Norwegian king Harald Hardrada's invasion of England, and was killed at the Battle of Stamford Bridge.

Godwin, Earl of Wessex: Godwin of Wessex (Old English: "Godƿin" ; 100115 April 1053) was one of the most powerful earls in England under the Danish king Cnut the Great and his successors.  Cnut made him the first Earl of Wessex.  Godwin was the father of King Harold Godwinson and Edith of Wessex, wife of King Edward the Confessor.
